content: Under the IMP regime used for Trojan analysis, for the same model and same IMP pruning path, the Trojan score being approximately zero for non-Trojan models, together with a significantly positive peak in the Trojan score along that IMP path indicating a backdoor-associated atypical pruning stability fingerprint, implies that computing the Trojan score along the IMP path yields a data-free detector of the pruning level where Trojan information is isolated, since the peak Trojan score characterizes the winning Trojan ticket.
